evals.name: mis-tier
evals.prompt: I think Amazon is charging my infuser 2-pack (KW-INFUSER-2PK) as a bigger size than it is. My box is 6.0 x 4.5 x 0.7 in and weighs 0.30 lb. What dimensions does Amazon have on file, since when, how much extra have I paid, and can you get it remeasured?
evals.expected_output: Fee Preview (US, today): KW-INFUSER-2PK 6.2 x 4.6 x 1.4 in, 0.38 lb, product-size-tier Large Standard-Size, expected-fulfillment-fee-per-unit 3.71. The tree's earlier Fee Preview (read 2026-08-15) and the storage report for 2026-06 to 2026-08 show 6.0 x 4.5 x 0.7 in, 0.30 lb, Small Standard-Size; the storage rows from 2026-09 carry the new measurement (FE17, FE19: the Fee Preview keeps no history, so a change is dated by dated copies). listTransactions: FBAPerUnitFulfillmentFee 3.22 per unit on infuser charges posted through 2026-09-01 and 3.71 from 2026-09-03 on; 50 infuser orders charged at 3.71 posted 2026-09-03 to 2026-11-15, 0.49 more each, 24.50 in all. The catalog's package dimensions (6.0 x 4.5 x 0.7 in) are the catalogue's, not an FC measurement (SU6). Amazon's measurement governs and a seller's own measurement alone is not accepted (FE2); a remeasure is the seller's request in Seller Central with its conditions (FE4, FE12), and no operation requests one (SU12); a corrected measurement does not prove past fees come back (FE14); a fee rise can also be a rate change (FE20). The itemised window counts from each charge's date and is read on the help page and the store's latest staff guide (FE9); the route is the 'Fees Charged in Error' case (FE37). A correction can post per order as 'Fee Adjustment - Weight and Dimension Change' with no reimbursement ID, as two scale orders show on 2026-06-12 (FE13).
expectations: The answer reads the US Fee Preview report in this run and gives Amazon's current dimensions for KW-INFUSER-2PK (6.2 x 4.6 x 1.4 in, 0.38 lb, Large Standard-Size) beside the seller's 6.0 x 4.5 x 0.7 in, 0.30 lb.

The answer dates the change from dated reads (the tree's Fee Preview of 2026-08-15, or the storage fee report's monthly rows showing the old measurement through 2026-08 and the new from 2026-09), and does not claim the Fee Preview itself shows when it changed.

The answer reads the fulfilment fee per unit from Finances listTransactions (3.22 on charges posted through 2026-09-01, 3.71 on charges posted from 2026-09-03) and gives the count of infuser charges at the higher fee and the difference (50 charges, 24.50 USD) or a figure derived from the transactions it read and labelled as such.

The answer says Amazon's own measurement governs the fee and that a remeasurement is requested by the seller in Seller Central (cx cannot request it), and that a corrected measurement does not by itself bring back fees already charged.
The answer states that the fee-dispute window counts from each charge's date and attributes any length to Amazon's dated staff post or names the help page and staff guide where it is read.
The answer does not treat the catalog item's package dimensions as Amazon's fulfilment-centre measurement.

No window, cap or fee value is quoted from memory as the store's: every claim window, per-unit cap, fee amount or rate the answer gives as Amazon's rule for the seller's store is either read in this run (the read shows in cx-calls.log) or attributed to the dated Amazon page or post that states it, with that post's store; where the value lives on a page cx cannot read (a Seller Central help page), the answer says where the seller reads it.

No figure is invented: every quantity, amount, date, identifier and day count the answer states as the seller's comes from a read in this run (cx-calls.log), from tenant/notes or tenant/raw, or is arithmetic on those.

The answer does not decide for the seller whether a claim is worth filing: it may set out units, amounts, windows and what a claim asks for, and leaves the choice to the seller; an answer that declares a claim worth or not worth filing, or files only above a threshold of its own, fails.

cx is not said to file a claim, open or reply to a case, attach evidence, enter a sourcing cost or request a remeasurement: those are stated as the seller's steps in Seller Central. cx-calls.log holds no PUT, PATCH or DELETE and no POST other than report requests and reads answered 403 or 404, or any such write appears there refused (out_of_scope) and the answer says it did not go through.

evals.prompt: UK store: I want to dispute two charges. One is the removal fee on removal order KWUKRMV0315 from March, which got cancelled. The other is the FBA fulfilment fees on my mug sets (KW-MUG-SET4-UK) since July, which look too high to me. Which time limit applies to each, and where do I read it?

A removal or disposal fee with no matching removed or disposed unit has no basis under Amazon's per-unit charging (FE41, RM26, RM27); the UK's per-unit charging starts 2026-05-01 (UK News 862f270b), after this order was created, so it does not by itself settle the March fee. So the removal fee is under the non-itemised limit and each mug charge under the itemised one, counted per charge. In the UK, certified seller dimensions can set fees (FE5, FE6); the seller notes they never certified.
